summary.intent: Focus on value for Callisto users by walking through the CLI as a new user would (init, add, status, version, PR body), noting rough edges, and fixing issues found, plus resolving review findings on an open PR.
summary.outcome: Fixed a review finding on the change-PR-links branch (a reused changeset name now keeps the newest PR, with a test and mutation check, committed, pushed and finding resolved). Also fixed never-released packages being reported as changed in the release preview, committed and pushed on fix/unreleased-needs-a-tag with docs updated and a PR link attempted.

repo: Callisto is a Rust workspace; relevant crates include callisto-graph (tags.rs, release_preview.rs, changeset_prs.rs), callisto-cli (integration tests in tests/emit_preview_tests.rs) and callisto-model.
`callisto init` needs `--yes` (plus e.g. `--versioning independent --no-workflow`) when run outside a terminal.
`callisto add` takes the package via `--package cargo/lib:minor --summary ...`, not a positional argument.
The changeset log is newest first, so for a reused changeset filename the first addition seen is the file that currently exists; use entry().or_insert rather than insert.
A package with no tag has no release baseline, so it should not be listed as 'Changed' in a first release PR preview.
The team uses mutation checks (scripts that revert the fix and confirm the new test fails) and a verify.sh script before committing; commits are GPG-signed (git commit -S) and verified via gh api.
Work is split across git worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ (change-pr-links, release-pr-token, unreleased-needs-tag).
Review findings are tracked with the `entire trail finding list/resolve` CLI and PRs are linked with `entire trail link`.

code.finding: Map building used insert, so older PRs overwrote newer ones for reused changeset names; changed to entry().or_insert to keep the newest, with test a_reused_changeset_name_keeps_the_newest_pull_request.
The publishable package list needed a filter on having a tag, so never-released packages are not reported as changed since release.
Existing test the_preview_lists_a_publishable_package_the_plan_leaves_out failed after the tag change and was updated to create a tag in its fixture repo.

friction: First walkthrough pass failed because init required --yes outside a terminal and add rejected the positional argument shape.
BSD sed in-place edit failed on macOS, requiring a switch to the Edit tool.
The untagged-package change broke an existing CLI test that assumed untagged packages were reported, requiring a fixture update.
Frequent EnterWorktree switching between multiple worktrees adds context-juggling overhead.
open_items: Check whether the new fix/unreleased-needs-a-tag branch merges cleanly with the feat/change-pr-links PR (#483); a merge-tree check was run but its result was not reported.
Confirm the entire trail link for the new branch succeeded and open or finish the PR.
The walkthrough covered status, version and PR body, but only the init/add issues and the first-release preview issue were addressed; remaining rough edges were not recorded in the transcript.
